This solution implies that the value of SLrho is constant on surfaces of constant energy HEUscript, in phase space. This is indeed the basic assumption of statistical mechanics. For example, in the microcanonical ensemble, the total energy E of an isolated system is specified. All members of the ensemble must then be located on the surface HEUscriptlparenoripcommaoriqrparenori = E in phase space. Equation (3.9) implies that a uniform density of points on this surface is stationary in time. The assumption of statistical mechanics is that the macrostate is indeed represented by such a uniform density of microstates. This is equivalent to replacing the objective measure of probability in Eq. (3.2) with a subjective one.

texts.orig: 4. The above postulate for SLrho eq answers the first question posed at the beginning of this chapter. However, in order to answer the second question, and to justify the basic assumption of statistical mechanics, we need to show that non-stationary densities converge onto the stationary solution SLrho eq . This contradicts the time reversal symmetry noted in point (1) above: for any solution SLrholparenoritrparenori converging to SLrho eq , there is a time-reversed solution that diverges from it. The best that can be hoped for is to show that the solutions SLrholparenoritrparenori are in the neighborhood of SLrho eq the majority of the time, so that time averages are dominated by the stationary solution. This brings us to the problem of ergodicity, which is whether it is justified to replace time averages with ensemble averages.
